home.title: Golden Hour: help in the first hour after a scam
home.lead: Lost money to an online scam? The first hour matters most.
home.helpSub: Step-by-step help for the next hour
home.checkSub: Check it before you reply, pay or click

footer.disclaimer: Not a government service. Not legal advice. Nothing you type here leaves your phone.

help.title: Lost money? Do these now
help.lead: Do them in this order. Even if hours or days have passed, still do every step.

steps.title: Call 1930
steps.body: Say you lost money in online fraud. Keep your bank SMS open: they will ask for the amount, the time and the transaction ID (UTR). Write down the complaint number they give you.

steps.title: Block your card and UPI
steps.body: Call your bank on the number printed on your card or shown in the bank's own app. Never use a number that came in a message or a search ad.

steps.title: Finish the complaint online within 24 hours
steps.body: On cybercrime.gov.in, choose financial fraud and enter your 1930 complaint number. Add screenshots of the transaction and the chat.

steps.title: Tell your bank in writing
steps.body: Use the bank app's fraud option or email the bank, and keep the complaint number. For frauds from 1 January 2027, tell your bank and 1930 within 5 days: small losses may then be compensated.

steps.title: Keep every proof
steps.body: Do not delete messages, chats, call logs or the scammer's UPI ID. Take screenshots now.

help.noLossBody: Report the call or message on Chakshu (sancharsaathi.gov.in) so the number can be blocked.

check.title: Check a message
check.label: Paste the message here
check.soon: The automatic checker is being built. Until then, stop if a message:
signs: asks for an OTP, PIN or password
asks you to pay first to get money, a job or a prize
threatens arrest, a blocked account or a cut connection, and rushes you
has a link or an app you were not expecting
check.copied: Copied. Paste it to someone you trust.
check.empty: Paste or share a message first.
check.shareIntro: Is this message real? Please take a look before I reply:

terms.title: Terms
body: Golden Hour is an independent open-source project. It is not run by or connected to the Government of India, I4C, RBI or any bank.
It gives general information from official public sources. It is not legal or financial advice, and it cannot recover money.
Always follow the instructions of the 1930 operator, the police and your bank.
The checker can be wrong. A message it does not flag can still be a scam.
Use it at your own risk. The software is provided as is, under the MIT licence.

privacy.title: Privacy
body: Golden Hour has no server that receives what you type, paste or share. Everything is processed on your phone.
The app keeps no history. A message you share to it is held only until the Check page opens, then deleted.
There are no accounts, cookies, ads or analytics.
Links to cybercrime.gov.in, sancharsaathi.gov.in and your phone dialer open outside the app.
